{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_114a5c10-678d-9cfa-808d-bfde092555dd","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"qwen3.8-max","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Root cause: a zero‑match scalar filter degenerates into “no filter at all” on the FTS path\n\nEverything below is **source‑based inference** from the snapshot at `/workspace` (zvec). I did not build or run the code, so no executed results are reported; all line references are to the snapshot as checked out.\n\n## 1. How the condition is classified and routed\n\nWith inverted indexes present, `status = 'archived'` / `views > 1000` are routed to the **invert** side of the query plan, not the forward side:\n\n- `SearchCondCheckWalker` sends a predicate on a field with `has_invert_index()` to `add_invert_filter()` (`src/db/sqlengine/analyzer/query_node_walker.cc:216`, `:701–704`); fields without an inverted index go to `add_forward_filter()` (`:694–699`).\n- `QueryAnalyzer::decide_filter_index_cond` lifts the invert sub‑tree into `query_info->set_invert_cond(...)` (`src/db/sqlengine/analyzer/query_analyzer.cc:276–287`); leftovers become `filter_cond` (`:304–307`).\n- The `InvertCondOptimizer` does not demote these to forward filters: `ratio_rule` returns `false` immediately for `EQ` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/optimizer.cc:39–45`), and for `GT` the evaluated ratio (0 matched of 3) is below `invert_to_forward_scan_ratio` (`optimizer.cc:84–87`). So the condition stays in `invert_cond_`.\n- Because the query has an FTS condition, the planner picks `fts_scan` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/query_planner.cc:413–415`, `:642–662`) and builds a `DocFilter` (`query_planner.cc:533–557`). With no forward predicate here, `forward_filter` is null and only `invert_cond_` is set in the `DocFilter` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/doc_filter.h:33–41`).\n\n## 2. What the inverted search returns for a zero‑match condition\n\n`DocFilter::compute_filter()` runs `InvertSearch::exec_invert_cond_tree` and stores `invert_result_` plus `invert_filter_ = invert_result_->make_filter()` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/doc_filter.cc:24–34`).\n\nFor the two zero‑match conditions:\n\n- `status = 'archived'` (EQ, term absent): `get_bitmap_eq` hits RocksDB `kNotFound` and returns a **null** bitmap (`src/db/index/column/inverted_column/inverted_column_indexer_search.cc:31–33`); `InvertedColumnIndexer::search` still wraps it into an `InvertedSearchResult` with `bitmap_ == nullptr` (`:810–815`). Crucially, `make_filter()` returns `nullptr` when `bitmap_` is null (`src/db/index/column/inverted_column/inverted_search_result.h:48–50`), and `count()` is 0 (`:79–85`).\n- `views > 1000` (GT, no matching ranges): `get_bitmap_gt` builds a **non‑null but empty** roaring bitmap (`inverted_column_indexer_search.cc:364`), so `count()` is 0 and `make_filter()` yields a filter that excludes everything.\n\nEither way, `invert_result_->count() == 0`.\n\n## 3. The bug: brute‑force‑by‑keys converts “matches nothing” into “unrestricted”\n\n`FtsRecallNode::prepare()` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/fts_recall_node.cc:110–141`) does:\n\n```cpp\nif (auto bf_keys = doc_filter_->get_bf_by_keys_and_update(\n        GlobalConfig::Instance().fts_brute_force_by_keys_ratio())) {\n  params.candidate_ids = std::move(bf_keys.value());          // line 126–129\n}\nparams.filter = doc_filter_->empty() ? nullptr : doc_filter_; // line 132\n```\n\n`DocFilter::get_bf_by_keys_and_update` (`doc_filter.cc:109–141`) computes `bf_by_keys_threshold = static_cast<uint64_t>(doc_count * ratio)`. With defaults (`fts_brute_force_by_keys_ratio = 0.05`, `src/db/common/config.cc:40`) and `doc_count = 3`, the threshold is `⌊0.15⌋ = 0`. A zero‑match condition has `match_count = 0 ≤ 0`, so the branch is **always** taken (for any ratio in [0,1], 0 ≤ threshold). It then:\n\n- `extract_ids(&ids)` → an **empty** vector (`doc_filter.cc:125–126`; `inverted_search_result.h:140–156` extracts nothing from a null/empty bitmap),\n- **clears** `invert_filter_` and `invert_result_` (`doc_filter.cc:127–128`; the comment at `fts_recall_node.cc:124–125` documents this clearing),\n- returns the empty vector, which becomes `params.candidate_ids`.\n\nNow both restrictions silently vanish:\n\n1. **Candidate restriction:** the FTS indexer applies candidate mode only when the list is non‑empty — `if (!query_params.candidate_ids.empty())` (`src/db/index/column/fts_column/fts_column_indexer.cc:209–217`), matching the contract comment “when non‑empty … restricts evaluation to this set” (`src/db/index/column/fts_column/fts_types.h:30–35`). An empty list is indistinguishable from “no candidate restriction”, so the term iterator for `hello` runs over **all** postings.\n2. **Push‑down filter:** after the clearing, `DocFilter::empty()` checks only pointers — `!(delete_filter_ || invert_filter_ || forward_plan_ || forward_filter_expr_)` (`doc_filter.cc:68–71`). `delete_filter_` is null because `SegmentImpl::get_filter()` returns `nullptr` when the delete store is empty (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:1613–1615`) and nothing was deleted; `invert_filter_` was just reset; no forward plan/expr exists. So `empty()` is `true` and `params.filter = nullptr` (`fts_recall_node.cc:132`), and the search loop runs unfiltered (`fts_column_indexer.cc:229–250`).\n\nResult: `hello` scores docs 1, 2, 3 into the min‑heap (`fts_column_indexer.cc:231–251`), passes through `SegmentImpl::fts_search` unchanged (`segment.cc:4585–4601`), and the query returns **{1, 2, 3}** — the zero‑match filter was erased rather than applied. (For the EQ case there is a second, latent route to the same outcome: even if the bf shortcut were disabled, `make_filter()` returned `nullptr` for the null bitmap — `inverted_search_result.h:48–50` — so `invert_filter_` would be null and `empty()` true anyway.)\n\n## 4. Why each control behaves correctly\n\n**Scalar‑only query (`status='archived'`) → empty.** With no vector/FTS condition the planner takes `invert_scan` (`query_planner.cc:416–418`, `:584–640`). `InvertRecallNode` iterates the `InvertedSearchResult` directly (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/invert_recall_node.cc:30–45`, `:82–85`). For a null bitmap, `InvertedIndexIterator` never becomes valid (`inverted_search_result.h:88–132`), so `gen()` immediately returns `std::nullopt` → empty set. Empty is *driven by the id set*, so “zero matches” naturally yields zero rows.\n\n**FTS `hello` + `status='published'` → {2, 3}.** `match_count = 2 > threshold 0`, so `get_bf_by_keys_and_update` declines (`doc_filter.cc:134–140`) and `invert_filter_` survives. `empty()` is false → `params.filter = doc_filter_`. During the posting walk, `next_doc(filter_ptr)` (`fts_column_indexer.cc:229–250`) calls `DocFilter::is_filtered` (`doc_filter.cc:73–86`), which delegates to `InvertedSearchResult::Filter::is_filtered = !contains(id)` (`inverted_search_result.h:39–41`) — doc 1 is excluded, docs 2 and 3 returned.\n\n**FTS `one` + `status='published'` → empty.** Same bitmap‑filter path; the only doc matching `one` (doc 1) is not in {2, 3}, so it is filtered out → empty intersection. This control shows the push‑down filter itself is correct; only the *empty match set* representation is broken.\n\n**No inverted indexes on `status`/`views` → empty.** The walker now routes the predicates to forward filters (`query_node_walker.cc:694–699`; `query_analyzer.cc:304–307`). In `build_doc_filter`, since `single_stage_search` is false (there was no invert cond before optimization, `query_planner.cc:391–397`), the forward expression is compiled into an Acero bitmap plan (`query_planner.cc:541–553`). `compute_filter()` materializes `forward_bitmap_` (`doc_filter.cc:36–49`); `get_bf_by_keys_and_update` returns `nullopt` because `invert_result_` is null (`doc_filter.cc:116–118`); `empty()` is false because `forward_plan_` is set → `params.filter = doc_filter_`. `is_filtered` reads the bitmap (`doc_filter.cc:80–86`, `:88–107`): all rows are `false` → every doc is excluded → empty set. The forward path never passes through the lossy “extract ids and clear” shortcut, which is why removing the inverted indexes *fixes* the anomaly.\n\n**Contrast with the vector path (informative).** `VectorRecallNode::prepare()` uses the same `get_bf_by_keys_and_update` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/vector_recall_node.cc:163–169`), but the keys travel as `bf_pks`, a `vector<vector<uint64_t>>` where a *present but empty* inner list is preserved (`vector_column_indexer.cc:184–193`: `bf_pks.size() == 1` → non‑null shared_ptr to an empty key list) and the core engine restricts the search whenever `bf_pks != nullptr` (`src/core/interface/index.cc:742–746`, `:871–874`). Presence‑vs‑absence is encoded by the pointer, not by list emptiness — exactly the distinction the FTS `candidate_ids` (a plain `std::vector`) loses.\n\n## 5. How the condition is classified and routed\n\nWith inverted indexes present, `status = 'archived'` / `views > 1000` are routed to the **invert** side of the query plan, not the forward side:\n\n- `SearchCondCheckWalker` sends a predicate on a field with `has_invert_index()` to `add_invert_filter()` (`src/db/sqlengine/analyzer/query_node_walker.cc:216`, `:701–704`); fields without an inverted index go to `add_forward_filter()` (`:694–699`).\n- `QueryAnalyzer::decide_filter_index_cond` lifts the invert sub‑tree into `query_info->set_invert_cond(...)` (`src/db/sqlengine/analyzer/query_analyzer.cc:276–287`); leftovers become `filter_cond` (`:304–307`).\n- The `InvertCondOptimizer` does not demote these to forward filters: `ratio_rule` returns `false` immediately for `EQ` (`src/db/sqlengine/planner/optimizer.cc:39–45`), and for `GT` the evaluated ratio (0 matched of 3) is below `invert_to_forward_scan_ratio` (`optimizer.cc:84–87`). With defaults (`fts_brute_force_by_keys_ratio = 0.05`, `src/db/common/config.cc:40`) and `doc_count = 3`, the threshold is `⌊0.15⌋ = 0`. A zero‑match condition has `match_count = 0 ≤ 0`, so the branch is **always** taken (for any ratio in [0,1], 0 ≤ threshold). It then:\n\n- `extract_ids(&ids)` → an **empty** vector (`doc_filter.cc:125–126`; `inverted_search_result.h:140–156` extracts nothing from a null/empty bitmap),\n- **clears** `invert_filter_` and `invert_result_` (`doc_filter.cc:127–128`; the comment at `fts_recall_node.cc:124–125` documents this clearing),\n- returns the empty vector, which becomes `params.candidate_ids`.\n\nNow both restrictions silently vanish:\n\n1. **Candidate restriction:** the FTS indexer applies candidate mode only when the list is non‑empty — `if (!query_params.candidate_ids.empty())` (`src/db/index/column/fts_column/fts_column_indexer.cc:209–217`), matching the contract comment “when non‑empty … restricts evaluation to this set” (`src/db/index/column/fts_column/fts_types.h:30–35`).
